arXiv:1911.02972.title: Blockwise Self-Attention for Long Document Understanding

arXiv:2201.11903.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models

Its central motivation and experiments focus on differentiability and training scalability; it reports inference throughput within −2.29% to +3.89% of conventional TopK MoE, i.e. roughly comparable speed rather than an inference-efficiency gain. Relevant MoE serving architecture, but evidence does not show inference reduction as its primary objective.
arXiv:2412.14711.title: ReMoE: Fully Differentiable Mixture-of-Experts with ReLU Routing

It contributes an evaluation checklist and empirical analysis rather than an inference-serving mechanism or an efficiency improvement itself. Retained as borderline because its object is LLM inference-system performance and reproducibility, while its contribution is methodological evaluation rather than system optimization.
arXiv:2507.09019.title: On Evaluating Performance of LLM Inference Systems

Retained as borderline because it includes LLM-agent loops while its objective/evaluation extends well beyond LLM inference.
arXiv:2510.04371.title: Speculative Actions: A Lossless Framework for Faster Agentic Systems

arXiv:2609.06128.title: Substrate-Portable Execution for Production LLM Workflows

arXiv:2609.08307.title: A Measurement Study of LLM Inference Trade-offs Across Edge Continuum Hardware

It is relevant to deploying quantized inference-time attention policies, but does not demonstrate inference latency, throughput or end-task gains; retained as borderline.
arXiv:2609.23585.title: Global Ranks Survive, Selected Heads Shift: BOS-Sink Topology under 4-bit Weight-Only Quantization

arXiv:2602.09721.title: Revealing the Challenges of Attention-FFN Disaggregation for Modern MoE Models and Hardware Systems
